finishes.note: The concrete box, 1.000 thick all round (walls, base, roof pierced r 2.750): hidden structure, never seen (Story: the Cube's box).

The six faces of light-field panel modules (0.700 pitch, 0.698 faces, 2 mm seams), Light's image luminaire: low-iron glass with a lenslet array over a black mask (Story: panel faces). Light draws the module housings from its record; this is their face.
The shaft's glass tube r 2.450-2.510, 60 mm laminated low-iron, 16 curved panes in four tiers (Story: shaft glass, laminated). No daylight reaches it: no UV interlayer needed.

The tier frames (r 2.410-2.450), the joint strips on the diagonals and the sleeve's joint line: oil gilt on CuSn10, clean (Story: joint lines, tier rings). Their upward faces take dust: the palette's 'dusted' is not a history yet (sheet 13).

The soffit ring in the ceiling (r 2.460-4.120, 30 mm, 4 mm drip) with its two beads, and the rail tails' brackets under it: oil gilt on CuSn10, clean (Story: soffit ring). The only gilt the black room shows besides the iris and the mast.
The sleeve r 2.450-2.750 through the void and the box's roof, two courses: CuSn10 patinated dark (Story: the one room where the future is black, because a light-field room must not reflect).
The iris housing (inner wall, roof, outer wall) and the soffit ring's hangers: CuSn10 patinated dark (Story: sleeve, iris housing, cavity plates).

The cavity's top and bottom plates and the three tier webs through the glass's tier joints (the glass stands on them; the graze lines hang under them): CuSn10 patinated dark, seen only through the glass.
The guide rails' brackets on the tier webs and on the sleeve: CuSn10 patinated dark (as built dark bronze).
The two guide rails and their tails below the iris (T-section, a rack on each back): machined steel, ground and hard-chromed, as the Atrium's and the Sphere's rails (ruled key).

The ceiling iris's blades (class iris.4600, 2 mm pearl steel as the other two iris.4600 closures), their upper faces seen from the shaft: oil gilt over the pearl lacquer (as built gilt; Story: gilt 'dusted on upward faces', a history the palette lacks).
The blades' undersides and edges, seen from the room round the mast head: oil gilt over the pearl lacquer, clean (as built gilt).
The hairline inlay along each blade's long edges on its upper face (7 mm, 0.4 mm proud): dark-patinated CuSn10, so the shut iris reads as a spiral from above (as built).
Site's blind on the plane z -0.500 while cube.up is unmated (the stand): the class closure shut, blades facing up (as the Atrium's atrium.down.blind-iris).

Hardcore under the Atrium's slab, -0.510 to -0.720 (mean): angular crushed limestone, compacted, dry. The cut face is consolidated in place, as a soil monolith is; the layer is the working (the palette's one key for the ground; records per layer are sheet 13).

Topsoil, -0.720 to -1.020 (mean): dark, crumbly, a little damp. The cut face is consolidated in place, as a soil monolith is; the layer is the working (the palette's one key for the ground; records per layer are sheet 13).

Subsoil, -1.020 to -1.500 (mean): paler, crumbly, damp. The cut face is consolidated in place, as a soil monolith is; the layer is the working (the palette's one key for the ground; records per layer are sheet 13).

The ammonite and the heart urchin in the chalk: chalk with an iron stain (as built linear 0.86, 0.74, 0.58 as a history, never a colour knob).
